newsitem.title: TONGA: Cyclone wreaks severe damage in Tonga.
newsitem.headline: Cyclone wreaks severe damage in Tonga.

text.p: The Pacific kingdom of Tonga was counting the cost of damage from Cyclone Hina on Monday after high winds tore roofs from houses and felled trees and power lines.
There were no immediate reports of casualties, but a Reuters correspondent in the capital, Nuku'alofa, said damage was extensive.

A large part of the wooden parliament's roof had been lifted off, and broken timber had crashed down inside, smashing pictures and falling onto tables. Iron roofing from shops was hanging from power cables like washing on a line.
Soldiers were using bulldozers to clear fallen trees from the road alongside the Royal Palace, while ordinary Tongans worked with bushknives to remove debris from minor roads.

All power was cut off, most businesses were shut down and schools were closed. Residents were fearful of food shortages later in the week, as refrigerated supplies would spoil unless electricity was restored quickly.

The cyclone was the latest of several to sweep through the South Pacific in recent weeks. Cyclone Gavin, which bore down on Fiji last week, left 10 people dead and 17 missing.
